guides.title: Move a Cloudflare Pages site off GitHub
guides.summary: Your site deploys to Cloudflare Pages from a GitHub repository. Bring the repository, issues and deploys to ForkMesh; Cloudflare keeps serving the site and your domain does not change.
steps: In the ForkMesh desktop app open Market, then Guides, and choose Install what you need on this guide.

On app.forkmesh.com open Repositories, choose New and pick GitHub as the source. Start resumable import brings issues, pull requests and history; Remote clone URL copies a public repository's code. For a private repository choose New repository and run git push --mirror to the address it shows.
In Cloudflare create an API token with the Cloudflare Pages: Edit permission and note your account ID.
In the desktop app open Settings, Secrets & Coves and add CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN, CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID and FORKMESH_ACTIONS_ALLOW_NETWORK set to 1.
Add .forkmesh/deploy.yml to the repository: on push to main, a job that runs your build (for example npm ci && npm run build) and then npx wrangler pages deploy dist --project-name=<your project>.
In the Cloudflare dashboard open the Pages project, then Settings, Builds & deployments, and turn off automatic deployments from GitHub so only ForkMesh deploys.
Push a commit and watch the run in Actions. Deploys that use secrets run on your ForkMesh desktop, so keep it signed in and online.
Open Status Page settings and add a monitor for your site's address so you hear when it goes down.

guides.title: Move a Vercel project off GitHub
guides.summary: Your app deploys to Vercel from GitHub. Keep Vercel serving it, and let ForkMesh hold the code, the reviews and the deploy button.
steps: In the ForkMesh desktop app open Market, then Guides, and choose Install what you need on this guide.
On app.forkmesh.com open Repositories, choose New and import the GitHub repository (or push a private one with git push --mirror to a New repository).
In Vercel create an access token under Account Settings, Tokens. Run npx vercel link once in a local checkout and copy orgId and projectId from .vercel/project.json.
In the desktop app open Settings, Secrets & Coves and add VERCEL_TOKEN, VERCEL_ORG_ID, VERCEL_PROJECT_ID and FORKMESH_ACTIONS_ALLOW_NETWORK set to 1.
Add .forkmesh/deploy.yml: on push to main, run npx vercel pull --yes --environment=production, npx vercel build --prod and npx vercel deploy --prebuilt --prod, each with --token=$VERCEL_TOKEN.
In Vercel open the project's Settings, Git and disconnect the GitHub repository so pushes there stop deploying.
Push a commit, follow the run in Actions, then add your production address as a Status Page monitor.

guides.title: Move a Netlify site off GitHub
guides.summary: Your site builds on Netlify from GitHub. Move the repository to ForkMesh and deploy to the same Netlify site from ForkMesh Actions.
steps: In the ForkMesh desktop app open Market, then Guides, and choose Install what you need on this guide.
On app.forkmesh.com open Repositories, choose New and import the GitHub repository (or push a private one with git push --mirror).
In Netlify create a personal access token under User settings, Applications, and copy the site ID from Site configuration, Site details.
In the desktop app open Settings, Secrets & Coves and add NETLIFY_AUTH_TOKEN, NETLIFY_SITE_ID and FORKMESH_ACTIONS_ALLOW_NETWORK set to 1.
Add .forkmesh/deploy.yml: on push to main, run your build and then npx netlify-cli deploy --prod --dir=<build folder>.
In Netlify open Site configuration, Build & deploy and stop builds from the linked GitHub repository.
Push a commit, follow the run in Actions, then add the site as a Status Page monitor.

guides.title: Move an AWS S3 + CloudFront site
guides.summary: Your static site lives in an S3 bucket behind CloudFront, deployed from GitHub or by hand. ForkMesh holds the repository and runs the upload and cache refresh for you.
steps: In the ForkMesh desktop app open Market, then Guides, and choose Install what you need on this guide.
On app.forkmesh.com open Repositories, choose New and import the repository from GitHub, GitLab or Codeberg, or push it with git push --mirror.
In AWS IAM create a user limited to s3:PutObject, s3:DeleteObject and s3:ListBucket on the bucket and cloudfront:CreateInvalidation on the distribution, then create an access key for it.
In the desktop app open Settings, Secrets & Coves and add AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, AWS_DEFAULT_REGION, CLOUDFRONT_DISTRIBUTION_ID and FORKMESH_ACTIONS_ALLOW_NETWORK set to 1.

Add .forkmesh/deploy.yml: on push to main, run your build, then aws s3 sync <build folder> s3://<bucket> --delete and aws cloudfront create-invalidation --distribution-id $CLOUDFRONT_DISTRIBUTION_ID --paths "/*".
Turn off the old GitHub workflow or CodePipeline that deployed the bucket so only ForkMesh writes to it.
Push a commit, follow the run in Actions, then add the CloudFront address as a Status Page monitor.

guides.title: Leave GitHub Pages
guides.summary: GitHub Pages only serves repositories that stay on GitHub. Move the repository to ForkMesh and publish the same files to Cloudflare Pages, which has a free plan and keeps your custom domain.
steps: In the ForkMesh desktop app open Market, then Guides, and choose Install what you need on this guide.
On app.forkmesh.com open Repositories, choose New and import the GitHub repository with its issues and pull requests.
In Cloudflare create a Pages project with direct upload, then an API token with the Cloudflare Pages: Edit permission.
In the desktop app open Settings, Secrets & Coves and add CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN, CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID and FORKMESH_ACTIONS_ALLOW_NETWORK set to 1.
Add .forkmesh/deploy.yml: on push to main, build the site if it needs it (a Jekyll site runs bundle exec jekyll build) and run npx wrangler pages deploy <output folder> --project-name=<your project>.
Add your custom domain to the Pages project, point its DNS at Cloudflare as the dashboard shows, then turn off GitHub Pages in the old repository's settings.
Add the address as a Status Page monitor.

guides.title: Move a Fly.io app's repository
guides.summary: Your server app runs on Fly.io and deploys from GitHub. Keep the machines on Fly.io and run flyctl deploy from ForkMesh Actions instead.
steps: In the ForkMesh desktop app open Market, then Guides, and choose Install what you need on this guide; it adds Sentry for error tracking too.
On app.forkmesh.com open Repositories, choose New and import the GitHub repository (or push a private one with git push --mirror).
Run fly tokens create deploy in a local checkout to get a deploy token for the app.
In the desktop app open Settings, Secrets & Coves and add FLY_API_TOKEN and FORKMESH_ACTIONS_ALLOW_NETWORK set to 1.
Add .forkmesh/deploy.yml: on push to main, run flyctl deploy --remote-only so the image builds on Fly.io's builders.
Delete the old GitHub workflow that ran flyctl deploy, push a commit and follow the run in Actions.
Add the app's health address as a Status Page monitor.
